text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.75% today to $135.64, giving back gains from earlier this week as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East escalated without lifting oil prices enough to offset profit-taking. Iran attacked U.S. military installations in Kuwait and struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, yet crude oil prices actually declined—U.S. oil fell below $90 a barrel—suggesting markets are pricing in either supply disruption concerns or investor nervousness that is weighing on energy stocks regardless of the headline risk.

The stock had climbed steeply from $137.86 just a week ago to $142.28 on November 13, so today's decline looks like a pullback after that rally ran its course. While the geopolitical backdrop remains volatile and the IEA warned of lost confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable energy corridor, oil traders are not yet translating that into higher prices—a signal that could keep near-term pressure on energy stocks even amid ongoing Middle East risks.
